CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right upper arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female presents with severe right upper arm pain after a fall during volleyball approximately 18 hours ago. Patient was attempting to spike the ball when an opponent kicked her legs from under her, causing her to fall and land on her right shoulder. Patient rates pain as 9 out of 10. She has been taking ibuprofen every 6 hours with minimal relief. No ice has been applied to the injury. X-ray imaging reveals a proximal humerus fracture.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies numbness or tingling in the right arm. Rest of systems reviewed and unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Gallstones.
Lumbar fusion approximately 6 years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen every 6 hours as needed.
Pepcid for gallstones.

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Plays recreational volleyball.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right shoulder: Swelling and erythema noted. Tenderness present over right shoulder. 
Range of motion: Able to straighten elbow when shoulder is not moved. Normal flexion at elbow.
Pulses: Normal bilaterally.
Neurologic: No numbness or tingling in right arm.
General: Rest of body examination normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right arm: Proximal humerus fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture, right arm. Most fractures of this type heal without surgery. Immobilization with long arm cast and sling prescribed. Follow-up x-ray in 2 weeks to assess bone realignment. If bones have not realigned, surgery will be considered at that time. Pain management with Lortab 5 mg 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed (20 tablets prescribed). Patient to proceed with casting.
